tb21_profile.skill: Drive a real interactive process through a pseudo-terminal: allocate a pty, spawn login/interactive bash, stream raw keystrokes including control/escape bytes, keep session state, and know tty echo/prompt/timing semantics
tb21_profile.domain: Python process control on Linux — pty/ptyprocess/pexpect, termios, fork+exec, signals, bash interactive startup files
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec: subclass a given abstract interface into an importable module, install deps, pass a hidden behavioural test suite

searches: tools.py search all "tmux|termios|tcsetattr|raw mode|screen session|ANSI escape|escape sequence" -n 25
tools.py search rts "\bexpect script|pexpect|spawn a|interactive shell|subprocess\.Popen|abstract base class|BaseTerminal" -n 25
tools.py search rts "execvp|fork a child|implements? a (simple )?(Linux |Unix )?shell|bashrc|PROMPT_COMMAND|readline" -n 30
tools.py search tmax "abstract base class|ABC\b|interface defined in|implement the .* interface|subclass" -n 15
tools.py search rebench "\btty\b|pseudo-?terminal|isatty|termios|/dev/pts|interactive shell|stdin is not a|subprocess" -n 25
tools.py show amoffat__sh-603 amoffat__sh-750 amoffat__sh-744 gorakhargosh__watchdog-946

TMax-15K.reason: Spawns an interactive bash under unshare and must drive it by prompt, handling shell readiness and clean exit — the exact crux.
Expect script that explicitly spawns a pseudo-terminal running /bin/bash and exports env into it; same pty-plus-bash mechanics.
Must write a reusable importable adapter module wrapping pexpect login/query flow — same shape: package interactive control behind an API.
Repairs and installs pexpect 4.8.0 from vendored source; forces reading pexpect internals and dependency install, both needed here.
Multi-step pexpect session against an interactive shell-like CLI: send, wait for prompt, verify state persists across commands.
Drives an interactive executable repeatedly via pexpect; teaches prompt matching and timeout handling that headless terminals need.
pexpect login sequence over a telnet console: username/password prompts then command mode — classic terminal state machine.
Full pexpect lifecycle automation of a prompting tool, including reading config and sequencing answers; same prompt-driven control loop.
Spawn a binary and bypass its interactive prompts programmatically; process spawning plus prompt discovery, though RE work dominates.
pexpect or subprocess pipe handling of a slow interactive installer under concurrency; teaches buffering and wait semantics.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Implements an interactive shell in C: prompt loop, fork+execvp, background jobs, exit — the process-control half of a headless terminal.
Same fork/execvp interactive shell with parent-does-not-wait background semantics; exercises child lifecycle reasoning directly.
Shell implementation requiring correct waitpid/background behaviour and error reporting for unknown commands.
Shell in C that must actually execute marker commands correctly, so the child's stdio wiring has to be right.
Same shell plus compile and permission steps; process control transfers, the packaging steps do not.
Shell implementation driven by a build-profile config; interactive command loop transfers, config plumbing is noise.
Interactive terminal program with per-keystroke state across a session; teaches stdin loop and session state, not ptys.
Interactive stdin decoder that must handle EOF and SIGINT cleanly — the signal/termination edge the \x03 test probes.
Interactive CLI game with stdin '-' support and shebang/exec bit; only weakly about terminal semantics.
PROMPT_COMMAND hook sourced by interactive bash; touches the rc-sourcing requirement but nothing about driving a pty.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Write an Expect script that spawns an interactive Python program and answers its prompts — same spawn/expect/send loop over a pty.
Implements an interactive shell in C with fork/execvp and background jobs; same child-process and prompt-loop reasoning.
Unix shell in C: parse input into argv, fork, exec, loop — the process-spawning core a headless terminal wraps.
Terminal menu driven by arrow keys, so the solution must read raw keys and decode escape sequences like \x1b[A.
Another fork/execvp shell where the parent must wait correctly; reinforces child lifecycle handling.
Interactive stdin program that must behave correctly on EOF and SIGINT — the interrupt path this task tests with \x03.
Must drive a program's interactive mode to build up state across many commands; same session-persistence requirement.
Run a program in interactive mode feeding an exact input sequence and capture full session output; prompt/response sequencing.
Extends a CLI to support an interactive session with stateful commands; the state-across-commands half of the interface.
Bash interactive-shell configuration persisted in .bashrc; only touches the rc-sourcing requirement, no process control.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Fix PtyProcess.waitnoecho — reasoning about tty echo attributes on a spawned pty is precisely what this implementation needs.
PtyProcess.isalive when the child dies by signal; same waitpid/status decoding a headless terminal must get right for Ctrl-C.
Signal handling plus subprocess pipe creation bugs; same class of child-process wiring and signal delivery reasoning.
ProxyCommand send/recv over a spawned subprocess: byte-level read/write against a live child, like the keystroke channel here.
Bug in the os.fork() child branch of worker spawning; forces correct reasoning about which side of a fork you are on.
Terminal helper regressions around ANSI escape sequences and terminal size — the escape-byte handling side of the interface.
Broken cursor movement and terminal output; debugging requires modelling what control codes do to a terminal.
Channel loses its context-manager base; restoring session-object lifecycle over an interactive channel is adjacent work.
curses monitor loop with keypress handling; same terminal-UI territory but the bug is in message formatting.
Shell-completion machinery for bash; shares the bash ecosystem but exercises no process or tty control.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Deadlock in sh's RunningCommand wait path; sh spawns commands on ptys, so this is exactly child-wait plus output-read ordering.
Signal-terminated processes and exit-code handling in a shell-command library — the Ctrl-C path this interface must support.
Output wrongly emits color control codes when stdout is not a tty; teaches when a stream is a terminal and why it matters.
watchmedo auto-restart regression: spawning, killing and signalling child processes and their groups correctly.
Crash on sys.stdout.isatty when no console is attached; forces handling of the no-terminal case in an exec/subprocess path.
Exit-code handling of spawned commands in sh; same process-result semantics the terminal wrapper must report.
Redirecting a spawned command's stdout/stderr to arbitrary sinks — the output-capture side of driving a child process.
Awaiting a running command object; concurrency around a live child process, close to timed send_keystrokes waits.
Open-mode handling in code vendored from pexpect/ptyprocess; brushes the library but the bug is filesystem faking.
Progress-bar state across fork and subprocesses; terminal output plus fork interaction, but shallow for this task.

final_top10.reason: Spawns and programmatically drives an interactive bash, handling prompts and readiness waits — same mechanism the interface must implement.
Repairs PtyProcess.waitnoecho: tty echo state on a spawned pty, the subtlety that breaks naive headless-terminal implementations.
Expect script spawning an interactive program and answering prompts; identical spawn/expect/send discipline in a different language.
isalive() after signal termination — the waitpid status decoding needed to make the Ctrl-C cancellation test pass.
Explicitly spawns a pseudo-terminal running /bin/bash and passes environment into it; same pty-plus-bash setup.
Packages pexpect interaction into an importable adapter module consumed by other code — same API-around-a-live-process shape.
Fixes and installs pexpect from vendored source, forcing a look inside the library this task would otherwise use blindly.
Implements an interactive shell with fork/execvp, background jobs and exit handling: the child-process control the wrapper hides.
Long multi-command pexpect session against an interactive shell, requiring state to persist between sent commands.
Deadlock between waiting on a child and reading its output in a pty-backed command library; the exact race a send/wait API hits.

notes: TMax is by far the strongest pool: it contains ~50 pexpect-driven interactive-automation tasks, of which the few that spawn an interactive bash (task_002893, task_005019) are the closest things in the whole corpus. SWE-Smith contains only two ptyprocess tasks but both are bullseyes on skill and domain and lose only on task_form, as the spec predicts. RTS is weak: apart from one heavily duplicated 'implement a shell in C' family and a couple of interactive-stdin programs, everything retrieved was boilerplate /app chores; ranks 9-10 there are filler. The lexical shortlist was badly polluted by 'interactive' matching deployment-prompt chores and by 'terminal'/'shell' matching bashrc/PATH setup; also note the rts 'echo vs printf escape sequences' family (200+ near-duplicates) is pure false positive for anything mentioning escape sequences.
